liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **To Lay Me Down** (2 reviews): This version of To Lay Me Down was later released on Reckoning; Reviewer found To Lay Me Down among the most peaceful moments of their life, and the acoustic sets unforgettable [9][10]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): This night's Franklin's Tower was later used on a Dead album; the title is cut off in the review; This upbeat, lyrically clean Franklin's Tower was the version chosen, in edited form, for the Dead Set album [9][12]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Reviewer calls this probably the best Dire Wolf of the tour [17]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Reviewer calls Half-Step perfect, with a magical second solo, and the segue into Franklin's stellar [17]
- **Black Peter** (1 other source): A very short patch covers the end of Black Peter [5]

## The recordings

- **gd80-10-25.aud.wiley.8726.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 31 songs; 205 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1980-10-25.120163.fob-nak700.gatto-jaeger.dan.flac16**: source not stated; 31 songs; 198 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this the best audience recording they've heard from the Radio City Music Hall run; The recording has little bass response in the mix [13][14]
- **gd1980-10-25.nak700.rolfe.miller.93804.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 31 songs; 207 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the Radio City recordings rough, blaming a hostile taping atmosphere around the two albums being produced [16]
- **gd1980-10-25.nak300.morrone.friend.116769.1644**: audience recording; 31 songs; 201 min [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended this show in person and remembers it as a good one [9]
- Reviewer and a friend named Bill hitched from UCONN to attend; they had been queuing for Rush tickets when the Radio City sale was announced [11]
- Reviewer believes this was meant to be opening night, but a quick sellout led to Friday being added [11]
- The New York crowd is very enthusiastic on the tape, and its energy seems to have lifted the band [14]
- Reviewer slept outside Radio City two days for front-row tickets, then crashed on the Merritt Parkway in heavy rain and spent two nights in jail, missing this show [15]
- Reviewer says others considered the 10/23 and 10/31 shows the best of the run, and questions whether Dead Set's Franklin's is from 10/31/81 [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-10-25.aud.wiley.8726.sbefail.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Audience recording transferred via MC and DAT to CDR, then seeded to etree by Tim W [1]
- **gd1980-10-25.120163.fob-nak700.gatto-jaeger.dan.flac16**: taped by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; transferred by Flac by Michael Turi, eq by Dan McDonald; source: Nak 700's > Sony D-5 > AMC; Recorded Dead front center loge by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; AMC > DAT > CDR > EAC > FLac (EAC > Flac by Michael Turi);… [4]
- **gd1980-10-25.nak700.rolfe.miller.93804.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Nakamichi 700 -> Master Cassette (Sony D5/Maxell UDXL-I & UDXL-II/Dolby B) [5]. Also: Transfer made from masters lent by Steve Rolfe; disc changes are seamless [5]
- **gd1980-10-25.nak300.morrone.friend.116769.1644**: taped by Tim Friend;Joe Morrone; transferred by AndrewF; source: AUD: 2x Nakamichi CM300/CP1 cardioids > Nakamichi 550 > Maxell UDXLII. Set up in second mezzanine few rows back, mics hand-held by Tim Friend, recording by Joe… [2]
